title: Competitor Workshop I
_note: DEMO CONTENT. All vehicle facts, needs, differentiators and the matrix solution are placeholders and must be replaced by the official CUPRA lists.

needs.text: Real-world range that covers the week without charging anxiety
Fast, uncomplicated charging on the go
A design that stands out and feels like a statement
Everyday practicality: space, boot, easy parking
Seamless connectivity and a modern digital cockpit
Driving fun: agile handling and immediate response
Performance that is felt, not just promised
Premium feel and quality at a fair price

differentiators.text: Up to ~450 km WLTP range in the long-range version
DC fast charging 10–80 % in under 30 minutes
Distinctive CUPRA design language with copper accents and sharp lines
Best-in-class rear legroom and boot for the segment
Large central display with CUPRA Connect app integration and wireless updates
Sport-tuned chassis with adaptive damping (DCC Sport) and progressive steering
VZ version with 226 hp, 0–100 km/h in under 7 seconds
CUPRA bucket seats and driver-focused interior at a lower price point than MINI

persona.name: Lena
persona.description: Lena lives in the city and commutes 40 km a day. She wants her first electric car to feel effortless: enough range for a spontaneous weekend trip, charging that does not eat her lunch break, and a car that does not look like everyone else's.

categories.title: Exterior & Design
prompts: Compare the front: which car makes the bolder statement? Look for the CUPRA signature lights and copper details.
Walk around both cars. Where does the CUPRA use sharper lines, and how does the R5 answer with retro cues?
Check wheel sizes and stance. Which car looks planted?

categories.title: Range & Charging
prompts: Find the charging port on both cars. Note the maximum DC charging power on the spec card.
Compare the WLTP range figures. What does the difference mean for Lena's weekend trip?
Look at the charging planner in the infotainment. How many steps to plan a route with a stop?

categories.title: Interior & Space
prompts: Sit in the rear of both cars behind a front seat adjusted for you. Where do your knees end up?
Open both boots. Which one takes a weekend bag plus groceries without folding seats?
Look at materials on the dashboard and door cards. Which feels more premium at eye level?

categories.title: Digital Cockpit
prompts: Pair a phone with each car. How many taps until navigation is on the screen?
Compare screen size and menu depth for the climate controls.
Ask about over-the-air updates: which car improves after purchase?

persona.name: Marc
persona.tagline: 42, enthusiast, second car for the family
persona.description: Marc drove hot hatches in his twenties and misses the feeling. The family car is covered, so this one is for him: it has to be fun on a back road, quick off the line, and feel special inside without costing MINI money.

categories.title: Chassis & Handling
prompts: Look at the ride height and tyre profile. Which car sits lower and wider?
Ask about adaptive damping. What does DCC Sport change for Marc on a back road?
Turn the steering wheel lock to lock in both cars. Which one feels more direct?

categories.title: Performance
prompts: Compare power output and 0–100 km/h on the spec cards.
Find the drive mode selector. How quickly can Marc switch to the sportiest mode?
Which car offers a dedicated performance version?

categories.title: Seats & Driver Position
prompts: Sit in both driver seats. Which one holds you in place when you lean sideways?
Check the steering wheel: material, thickness, paddles or drive-mode buttons.
Compare the view over the bonnet. Which car feels more like a cockpit?

categories.title: Price & Value
prompts: Compare the list prices on the spec cards for comparable power.
Which features are standard on the CUPRA that MINI charges extra for?
What does Marc get for the difference?
